status: MEASURED — the noise-to-signal ratio replaces the (retracted) isotropy assumption, and it agrees with the independent Spearman-Brown extrapolation to within 5%

design.xi_i: (phi_i - b) * s_i, s_i = dose-unit gradient along rollout i, b = global mean phi (estimated, not corrected)

N1_noise_scale.verdict: PASS — two independent routes to the crossover agree

N2_pred_vs_measured.verdict: level and flatness reproduced; worst point is K=8 (3x), endpoint K=32 within 5%

key_arithmetic.dimension_comparison: K* = 1500 is 197x SMALLER than the ambient dim 294912 — so 'K ~ d' was wrong in exactly the direction the literature predicts (low-rank gradients, arXiv:2407.11239, Aghajanyan et al. 2021)

verdict: The flat r(K) is now explained by a measured number instead of an assumption: the noise-to-signal ratio is 1500, so r(K) ~ K/1500 in the small-r regime and 32 rollouts can only give r ~ 0.02. Reaching r = 0.5 needs ~1500 rollouts per context. The ambient dimension is irrelevant at this scale (K* is 197x smaller than dim), which is consistent with the anisotropy/low-rank literature and inconsistent with the isotropy reading now retracted.
caveats: b is the global mean phi, itself estimated from the same 256 samples and not corrected for (biases g_sq downward, i.e. makes K* an upper-ish estimate)
single seed; the per-context sum of ||xi||^2 spans 5.2e7..1.4e9 (ctx 6 is 27x ctx 5), so the trace is dominated by a few contexts and a per-context K* would be more honest than a pooled one
no independent check that the 256 xi_i are uncorrelated (the ANOVA split assumes it)
